The *Uppādanirodhavāra* ("Section on Origination and Cessation") is a canonical text belonging to the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. Positioned within the *Āyatanayamaka* (the third major division of the work), it forms the third subsection of the process division (*pavattivāra*), which systematically interrogates its doctrinal categories through a threefold scheme: origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and simultaneous origination and cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Ronkin 2005].

Scholars observe that the process sections of the *Yamaka* chapters reflect early Buddhist process metaphysics, treating experiential phenomena as dynamic processes rather than substantial entities [Ronkin 2005]. Doctrinally, these sections mark a critical milestone in the development of the Abhidhamma theory of momentariness, providing what is likely the earliest canonical occurrence of the term *khaṇa* in the sense of the subdivision of an experiential moment into sub-moments of origination (*uppādakkhaṇa*) and cessation or destruction (*bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Ronkin 2005].

 According to DharmaNexus text-reuse analysis, the *Uppādanirodhavāra* shares 14,411 matching passages with 36 Pali texts, showing massive formulaic overlap with other *Yamaka* sections [DharmaNexus]. Its highest internal reuse occurs with adjacent sections of the *Āyatanayamaka*—specifically *Uppādavāra* (Ya 3.2.1) and *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 3.2.2)—as well as corresponding process sections in the *Indriyayamaka* (Ya 10.2.1) and *Khandhayamaka* (Ya 2.2.3) [DharmaNexus]. Shared passages are also documented in the sub-commentarial tradition, including the *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* and *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further registers cross-language alignments with northern Buddhist scholastic works, such as Tibetan translations of the *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* and Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā*, though these machine matches reflect common Abhidharmic terminology rather than direct textual parallels [DharmaNexus].
